senses.gloss: (b. h.) to burst forth; to be bright, shine. V. גִּיהַּ a. גִּיחַ.

units: <cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 38">Pirké d’R. El. ch. XXXVIII</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 18">Yalk. Josh. 18</cite> [read:] <he>היתה אבנו מַגִּיהָה את אורה</he> its (the tribe’s) jewel shed its light; a. e.

senses.gloss: (cmp. Hif. of נָבַט) to look over; to revise a manuscript, to correct, restore (when faded).
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 13a:24">Ber. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>בקורא להַגִּיהַּ</he> when he reads for the sake of revising. Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵇ bot. (in a misplaced passage) <he>אם להגיה כדי להגיה וכ׳</he> (not <he>להגות</he>) if (he carries ink) for the purpose of correcting, (he is guilty when carrying) enough to correct one letter.

<cite ref="Ketubot 106a:9">Keth. 106ᵃ</cite> <he>מַגִּיהֵי ספרים וכ׳</he> the official revisers of Biblical manuscripts; Y. Shek. IV, 48ᵃ top <he>מַגִּיהֵי ספר העזרה</he> (Bab. ed. Var. <cite ref="P00426"><he>עזרא</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) the revisers of the Temple manuscript.

<cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 3:4">M. Kat. III, 4</cite> (<cite ref="Moed Katan 18b:24">18ᵇ</cite>) <he>אין מַגִּיהִין אות אחת אפי׳ בספרי העזרה</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>בספר עזרא</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) we dare not (during the festive week) correct (restore) one letter even in the Temple books (ed. in the manuscript named after Ezra).
Meg. II, 2 היה … ומַגִּיהָהּ if he recited the Book of Esther while he was writing or teaching or correcting it; a. fr.—Part. pass. מוּגָּהּ revised, correct.
<cite ref="Pesachim 112a">Pes. 112ᵃ</cite> <he>כשאתה … למדהו בספר מ׳</he> when thou teachest thy son, teach him from a corrected book.
<cite ref="Ketubot 19b:4">Keth. 19ᵇ</cite> <he>ספר שאינו מ׳</he> an unrevised Bible manuscript.
